_comment: DIR-125 replay fixture: the high-value finding classes actually observed across the 10 real DIR-120/M192 prepare-milestone attempts (8→2→1→1→1→2→2→1→2→1), reshaped into ONE typed full-review round. Two are genuinely blocking (missing production-behavior AC coverage; stale acceptance wiring); the other four are valuable but non-blocking and must survive with an explicit disposition rather than being discarded or re-triggering a full Proposal regeneration.

findings.summary: Phase 3b is a second, independently landable mechanism and should be split into its own task (the real DIR-026 split that produced DIR-120-B).
findings.evidence: Phase 3b touches an unrelated subsystem and has its own AC/DoD shape.

findings.summary: A new production behavior change has no falsifiable Acceptance Criteria item covering it.
findings.evidence: Proposal claims a new fail-closed default but no AC item asserts it mechanically.

findings.summary: The task's extra.acceptance command still points at an earlier milestone (M186) instead of the current one.
findings.evidence: extra.acceptance references M186-*.md; the current milestone is M192.

findings.summary: Missing a named regression test for the touch-set change.
findings.evidence: No test file named for the new touch path in the Plan.

findings.summary: An operator-facing pointer in OUTER-LOOP.md still names the old script path.
A rarely-hit fallback branch is not exercised by any test; accepted as a known, low-probability risk rather than blocking preparation.
findings.evidence: Fallback branch guards an already-validated invariant; adding a dedicated test is disproportionate for this milestone's scope.
